summary: Numerical quantifiers relative to the identity criteria of common nouns, after section 5.3 of the book. The numeral is 'at least n' for every n: n objects, pairwise distinct under the criterion, all satisfying the predicate. Counts transfer along a sub-setoid and not without inheritance of the criterion; under a dot-type the count is by double distinctness, which gives both separate counts and is not given by them; an adjective inside a Sigma-type moves into the predicate. Three closed models, among them two copies of one content: exactly two books physically, exactly one informationally.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. ISTE/Wiley.

theorems.name: S1_three_is_at_least_3
theorems.source_claim: S1_three_is_at_least_3. The book's three-variable numeral is the generic numeral at 3.

theorems.name: S2_three_is_three0_on_restriction
theorems.source_claim: S2_three_is_three0_on_restriction. Def 5.4 with a setoid B restricts to Def 5.3 over the sub-setoid: counting A-objects by B's criterion is counting in (A, kB restricted).

theorems.name: S3_sub_setoid_transfer
theorems.source_claim: S3_sub_setoid_transfer. (5.26), for every n: if (A, kA) is a sub-setoid of (B, kB), then n A's that P entail n B's that P.

theorems.name: S4_transfer_needs_inheritance
theorems.source_claim: S4_transfer_needs_inheritance. Without inheritance the transfer fails: a subtype whose criterion is finer than the restriction (passengers counted by trips, persons by persons). There are two passengers and not two persons.

theorems.name: S5_downward
theorems.source_claim: S5_downward. Numerals are downward closed: n+1 entails n.

theorems.name: S6_monotone
theorems.source_claim: S6_monotone. Upward monotone in the predicate and along a further coercion.

theorems.name: S7_dot_is_pre
theorems.source_claim: S7_dot_is_pre. The dot relation is a pre-setoid relation when its components are.

theorems.name: S8_dot_not_transitive
theorems.source_claim: S8_dot_not_transitive. It is not an identity criterion: transitivity fails even when both components are equivalences (the book's remark after Def 5.6).

theorems.name: S9_dot_double_distinctness
theorems.source_claim: S9_dot_double_distinctness. (5.48), for every n: counting under the dot relation is counting objects that are distinct under both components.

theorems.name: S10_copredication_splits
theorems.source_claim: S10_copredication_splits. Copredication entails the two separate counts.

theorems.name: S11_split_does_not_join
theorems.source_claim: S11_split_does_not_join. The converse fails: "John picked up three books and mastered three books" does not entail "John picked up and mastered three books".

theorems.name: S12_sigma_absorbs_adjective
theorems.source_claim: S12_sigma_absorbs_adjective. (5.52)-(5.55): the adjective inside the Sigma-type moves into the predicate. "Three heavy books" counts books that are heavy; no premise on proofs of "heavy" is needed, because objects are compared by the...

theorems.name: S13_reflexivity_needed
theorems.source_claim: S13_reflexivity_needed. Why a pre-setoid relation must be reflexive: with an empty relation, one object counts as two.

theorems.name: S14_counting_form
theorems.source_claim: S14_counting_form. Counting form: on a finite listing, with decidable criterion and predicate, "at least n" holds iff the P-objects fall into at least n classes.

theorems.name: copies_counted_phy
theorems.source_claim: A use of S14_counting_form: the two-copies model, decided by counting.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
The book defines the numeral for three; the file states each result for every n and proves that the book's three-variable form is the instance at 3.
The dot-type is a product, which is all that counting needs; the book's rules for dot-types are not formalized.
